title: Zephaniah
summary: Zephaniah is a biblical book focused on the day of the Lord, judgment, remnant humility, and restoration joy.
historical_context: Zephaniah announces the Lord's searching judgment and ends with a restored, rejoicing remnant.
ancient_near_east_context: Zephaniah belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Zephaniah should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Zephaniah as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Minor Prophets, book 9 of 12, Zephaniah contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting the day of the Lord, judgment, remnant humility, and restoration joy to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Zephaniah as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Zephaniah uses prophecy, poetry within Minor Prophets, book 9 of 12 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Zephaniah helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional prophetic attribution to the named prophet
Many scholars recognize collection and editorial shaping
date_ranges: 8th-5th centuries BCE, depending on the prophet
Final forms often reflect later collection and editing
original_audience: Israel and Judah under covenant accountability before and after exile
historical_setting: Assyrian, Babylonian, and post-exilic settings across the prophetic corpus
canonical_role: Zephaniah anchors the day of the Lord, judgment, remnant humility, and restoration joy within Minor Prophets, book 9 of 12 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How to read prophetic poetry, irony, and symbolic action

related_objects.notes: The day of the Lord is central to the book.
Judgment against Judah and the nations shapes the prophecy.
A humbled remnant becomes the hope after judgment.
The book ends with restoration and rejoicing.
The prophecy emphasizes the Lord's justice.

scripture_references.notes: the day of the Lord as judgment

interpretive_notes.note: Read Zephaniah first within its own literary setting before moving to broader canonical connections.
